findings.problem: load_metrics fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), domain parsing, and result construction in a single function. Data/Calculations/Actions architecture requires the shell to handle I/O and pass parsed data to pure calculation logic.
findings.failure_mode: The function cannot be unit-tested without a real file on disk; I/O side effects leak into what should be pure metric-loading logic, making the core untestable and unprovable.
findings.fix: Split into a shell function that reads the file and a pure parse_metrics(input: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that takes a string and returns typed errors.

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() is a panic surface on file-not-found, permission-denied, or I/O errors. Absolute law forbids unwrap in production.
findings.failure_mode: Missing or unreadable metric file causes a process panic instead of returning a typed, recoverable error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err or a match on fs::read_to_string to produce typed I/O errors.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric value. Absolute law forbids unwrap in production.
findings.failure_mode: A single malformed line in the metrics file aborts the entire load instead of returning a typed parse error for that record.
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| ParseError::Invalid(name.clone(), e))? and return a typed ParseError::Invalid variant.

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 is a lossy cast. Values in range 65536..=4294967295 silently truncate to u16. Absolute law forbids lossy as casts.
findings.failure_mode: A metric value of 70000 silently becomes 4464, corrupting data without any error or warning.
findings.fix: Parse directly to u16 with .parse::<u16>().map_err(...), or use u16::try_from(u64_value).map_err(ParseError::Overflow) for checked conversion.

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on a split result. A line with zero comma-separated fields will panic.
findings.failure_mode: An empty line or a line with no commas causes an index-out-of-bounds panic.
findings.fix: Use parts.first().ok_or(ParseError::Empty) and parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingField) with match or ? operator.

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing. A line with only one field (name only) will panic.
findings.failure_mode: A metric line missing the value field causes an index-out-of-bounds panic instead of a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::MissingField) with map_err on the parse result.

findings.problem: No try_reserve or domain cap on the number of records. The function collects arbitrary line counts into an unbounded Vec with no capacity validation.
findings.failure_mode: A large or malicious file can cause unbounded memory allocation, leading to OOM or denial of service.
findings.fix: Validate a domain max_rows cap before iterating; use Vec::new() then out.try_reserve(bound).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?; enforce max_rows on each push.

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String. Domain names carry invariants (non-empty, no whitespace, valid characters) that are never enforced. Raw primitives in domain types break the parse-don't-validate principle.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct Record with empty strings, whitespace, or arbitrary text, violating domain invariants silently.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype MetricName(String) with a smart constructor fn MetricName(s: String) -> Result<MetricName, ParseError> that validates non-empty and character constraints.

findings.problem: Raw String primitives from fs::read_to_string cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors. The core consumes unvalidated raw data, so callers and upstream can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed metric lines (empty names, non-numeric values, extra fields) produce panics or silent truncation instead of typed domain errors.
findings.fix: Parse at the boundary: read raw text in the shell, then call a pure parse_metrics(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> that validates every field with fallible smart constructors and returns a typed error taxonomy.

findings.problem: No typed error type exists. All failures (I/O, parse, validation, allocation) are collapsed into panic surfaces. There is no error taxonomy.
findings.failure_mode: Callers cannot distinguish between a missing file, a malformed line, or an out-of-range value, preventing correct error handling and recovery.
findings.fix: Define enum ParseError { Io(io::Error), Empty, Invalid(String, std::num::ParseError), MissingField(usize), Overflow, Allocation }; define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError) }.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds logging I/O inside the parsing/mapping closure. Core calculation logic must not perform I/O.
findings.failure_mode: Metric loading produces console output as a side effect, contaminating pure data transformation and making the function unsuitable for batch processing or testing.
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing closure. If metrics need reporting, emit it in the shell layer after parsing completes, or return a diagnostic result alongside the records.

findings.problem: text.lines() iterates over all lines with no static upper bound or domain cap on iteration count.
findings.failure_mode: A file with billions of lines causes unbounded processing time and memory allocation.
findings.fix: Add a domain cap on max_records; use enumerate() with a check idx >= max_records returning ParseError::TooMany.

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for load_metrics. No baseline measurement, workload definition, or performance claim is present.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics of file reading, string splitting, Vec allocation, and parsing are unknown; regressions go undetected.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or custom benchmark measuring file read time, parse throughput (records/sec), and memory allocations for small, medium, and large input files.

findings.problem: No evidence that cargo fmt --check, cargo check, cargo clippy, or cargo test were executed. Review cannot verify zero-warranty compliance.
findings.failure_mode: Formatting drift, clippy warnings, or compilation failures may exist unreported.
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt --check, cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features, cargo clippy with strict lints, and cargo test, then report results.

findings.problem: Each line allocates a Vec<String> for split parts plus individual String allocations for each trimmed part, then clones into Record. No allocation budget or profiler data.
findings.failure_mode: Per-record allocation pattern causes GC pressure and cache misses at scale; no measurement proves this is acceptable.
findings.fix: Profile with alloc_counter or similar to quantify per-record allocations; consider borrowing from the line string or using a fixed-capacity temporary buffer.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics throughput or allocation characteristics
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, cachegrind, or alloc counter) for the hot path
no cargo fmt --check, cargo check, cargo clippy, or cargo test command evidence
no allocation budget or memory profiling for the parse-and-collect pipeline
no second-ring evidence tying any performance claim to measured symbols or artifacts
residual_risk: This crate contains 12 blocker-level violations of absolute Holzman laws: panic surfaces (unwrap), unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden I/O in pure logic, unbounded allocation, missing typed error taxonomy, raw domain primitives, and no parse boundary. The code cannot be delivered until all blockers are repaired. Even after repair, benchmark, profiler, and command-evidence gates remain unfulfilled.
